utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. O'Sullivan, I note the absence of Mr. Milutinovic, but I note also that there's a waiver to proceed with today's hearing. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just wanted to indicate, we have a new face on the Prosecution side this day. Assisting our case manager Susan Grogan is Tamara Margitic, who may join us later on during the trial as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Ramadani.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The evidence will now continue. Please remember that the solemn declaration which you made at the beginning of your evidence to tell the truth will continue to apply to your evidence today, and the next counsel to ask you questions will be on behalf of Mr. Lazarevic, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. And since you have introduced me, there's no need for me to introduce myself again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ramadani, I have just a couple of questions for you and I believe that we will go through them rather quickly, if your answers are short and precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to place on the screen P99.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, do you have that document on the screen?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If you could enlarge it a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it now good?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, I have to put on my glasses first. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, yesterday we saw this photo on a number of occasions and I have just one question about this photo. Could you please tell us whether you can see the main road, the Djakovica-Prizren road, in this photo.

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The main road, Gjakova-Prizren, is not on this photo, because it goes by the end -- by the edge of the village. Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And in the upper right corner, in the top part of the photo, can you see at least a part of that road?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this here, this is part of the road, yes, Prizren-Gjakova, but it's only part of it. It's not very clear from this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you mark the very top of the photo with a blue marker, the top of the photo where you can see the part of the road. Or just draw a line.

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, the cellar. Here I think. This here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ramadani. Could you please put number 1 next to that dot, or maybe the dot will be enough. Okay, number 1. Tell me, please, can you see your house in this photo? Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My house, this one here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you please put number 2 next to it in order to make things clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Ramadani. Yesterday you also showed us the stream where you were. You also pointed for us the house.

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the stream is around here, but it's not --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You don't have to show us that; we already have that. Mr. Ramadani, you don't have to do it again; we already have one photo the stream, of the house, belonging to Mr. Batusha and the place where Mr. Batusha's cowshed is. You pointed all that for us yesterday. You will agree with me that from these three places, given the fact that we see the houses that are densely placed in the corner, that you could not see all these places from the main road, the places that we have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, in the corner, you can see the road. You can see also downwards towards the stream and the meadow, but upwards you cannot see, upwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ramadani.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this photo be given an exhibit number, please? Then I will move on.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC68, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, thank you very much. You don't have to look at this photo anymore. I have before me the transcript of your testimony in the Milosevic case. Is it true that in that case you stated that, as far as Mala Krusa goes, the Albanians did not die at the hands of the Yugoslav army and that the same apply to the neighbouring village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Could we have a page reference for that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The page is 6723, lines 16 through 22.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, but I did not understand the question very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I referred you to the page, and I'm asking you whether it is correct that in the Milosevic case you stated that the Albanians did not die at the hands of the Yugoslav army in Mala Krusa, and that the same was true of the neighbouring villages. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to this because, as far as I see from the transcript, the question put by Mr. Milosevic referred to whether any Albanians were killed by NATO bombing. It doesn't talk about the army at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the question was this: "If nobody was killed by the KLA in fighting, if nobody was killed by NATO, all who perished, according to you, were civilians, the civilians that died at the hands of the Serbian police and the Serbian army." The civilians were mentioned and Mr. Ramadani responded in reference to the civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What was the response? I don't have this transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The response was: "The Albanians died at the hands of the Serbian police in Mala Krusa and the same was true of the neighbouring villages." I believe that the objection is not founded and that a clear reference is made to the Albanian civilians, and the response as well refers to the Albanian civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't see any reference in the answer to neighbouring villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a moment. The problem here is created by the approach to the question. The transcript's quite unnecessary for the question you want to ask, and it's only if you get an answer that you think is inconsistent with what the witness has said before in court that there's any point in going into the transcript. And that's why confusion's arising often in relation to this type of question. So why don't you put the basic question, and then if it needs to be tested by reference to the transcript, we can go back to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that that is the question that I put, and this was followed by an objection. The only thing I said was that the witness had already spoken about that. Let me put the question to Mr. Ramadani.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, is it true that in Mala Krusa and in the neighbouring villages, the Albanians did not perish at the hands of the Yugoslav army?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Innocent civilians were killed by the police; the police killed them and burned them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, is it also true that the artillery was not used in Mala Krusa during the period of time that you're terrifying about?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was used. The army was all around Krusha e Vogel, outside the village not inside the village. I said earlier that inside the village the police were there, while the army was around, all around the village. There were Pragas and tanks, but the APCs were inside on the streets of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, I'm going to read back to you what you said at the Milosevic trial. Page 6721 of the transcript, lines from 21 through 24, the accused Milosevic asked you: "Very well, then. Was the artillery used or was it not used? Can you tell me that?" "JUDGE MAY: The witness said that the artillery was not used." The witness Ramadani answered: "The artillery was not used. There was only shooting from armoured vehicles." What is correct, what you said during the Milosevic trial or what you are saying to us today? The question was very clear and your answer was clear as well; you said that the artillery had not been used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, before you -- sorry, please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said it earlier and I said it yesterday that the artillery, the army was around the village, around the village but not inside the village. I'm testifying here about my village, not other villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, did the army fire these artillery weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not see them use those weapons, but they cleansed the terrain. And the militia, the police, opened fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: One other thing you said according to the Milosevic transcript was: "There was only shooting from armoured vehicles." What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, from the APCs. But the tanks and the Pragas were around the villages, while on the APCs, they had guns on them and they opened fire on the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, you also provided a statement on the 5th of October, 2001. Is that correct? This was provided to the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've given many statements, but I didn't keep notes when I gave those statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, let me read to you a part of your statement relative to what we have just spoken about. "They asked me how many vehicles of the VJ were to be seen on the asphalt road outside of Mala Krusa. They were lined up along the Djakovica-Prizren road, the asphalt road. The first time they were deployed there was on the 25th of March at 4.00. And the vehicles that I saw were something between the APCs, the armoured vehicles and Pragas, and they were not camouflaged. The APCs were of blue colour; they belonged to the MUP. And the Pragas were of a regular green colour, as in the VJ. They asked me if I knew whether a T-55 was ever stationed in the area of Mala Krusa." And your answer was no. In other words, in the statement you provided, as I've already said, on the 5th of October, 2001, you denied having seen a VJ tank. You only saw Pragas and APCs. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In every statement that I gave, I've said that the tanks and the Pragas were stationed on the main road Prizren-Gjakova and around the village. There were tanks and Pragas, while the APCs were on the streets inside the village. I don't know how to explain this any further. I think it's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, I understand your explanation and I have no further questions about that. My last question to you is this: Did you give your statement, and the question put to you was whether you had seen a tank in that area, in the territory of Mala Krusa, and your answer was no, very clear and loud. And if you don't have any other explanations save for us, I have no further questions for you, sir.

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My house is in the outskirts of the village and you can see the asphalt road very well from there. And I'm saying this again today: There were tanks there and Pragas.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions for this witness. And I assume, Your Honours, that the transcripts and the statement that I have referred to, since they have been used, that they will automatically be admitted into evidence, that I don't have to tender them specially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the transcript so far as relevant is already in as 6D87, but I don't think the statement is and we don't have a number from the further statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this may be a convenient moment for this. My case management wanted to put this on e-court, but team 6D has already done that. I have their number, which is 6D87. Maybe to avoid duplication -- sorry, and the statement is 6D82. 6D82 is the statement that I have discussed with Mr. Ramadani.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could we see on the screen the point that you've just put to him, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So can we see 6D82? Now, do you know which e-court page number has the final question that you put?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know what you have in the system, and the page numbers are the same. It's number 3. More specifically, what I have read out can be found in the last paragraph on that page. The question is the fifth line from the bottom of the page and the answer follows immediately after that. There was also a question about rockets, whether rockets were seen on those vehicles, and the answer was also no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But the specific question here was whether he was aware of any T-55 tanks being stationed in Mala Krusa at this time. Is that right? Right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would just like to note that Mr. Bakrac also read out the paragraph which is now at the very top of the page, to the witness -- no, it was at the top in the position it was just now. Yes, now you have scrolled up again. "I have also been asked how many ..." This was also read out to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Thank you. Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ramadani, I'm Tomislav Visnjic, Defence counsel for General Ojdanic, and I'm going to put a few questions to you. Actually, I need some clarification from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown P99, page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, this is also a photograph of your village taken from another angle from which the asphalt road can be seen a bit better, the one that we talked about, the road between Prizren and Djakovica. My question is the following: In this photograph, can you mark the place where Batusha's cowshed was.

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Prizren-Gjakova main road. Here. This is where the Batusha cowshed is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: All right. Is it correct, Mr. Ramadani --

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Yes, it is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: -- is it correct that from the asphalt road between Prizren and Djakovica one cannot see this yard and Batusha's house, let alone Batusha's cowshed? Am I right? Two reasons at that, the first being that it's in the hills and pretty far away; and the second reason is that even if something could be visible, the houses before that block the view and the trees that are pretty high there. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You cannot see the house from the asphalt road, but you can see it from Suka Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: That's right. That's on the other side of the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Has the photograph been marked? Because it's not come up on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is a blue dot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps it would be a good thing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- if the witness put a number 1 by the dot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Before you go on, Mr. Visnjic. Mr. Ramadani, you've told us that there were armoured vehicles on the main road and you've also said that the army's tanks and Pragas, as you put it earlier, were all around the village. Now, can you indicate on this photograph what you mean by "all around the village"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is my house here, and you can see the asphalt road from the second floor. When we woke up at 4.00, we saw everything on this asphalt road, the tanks, the Pragas. So from this house you can see the asphalt road and Suka Brdo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, does that answer mean that these vehicles were simply on the main road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have exhausted the topic in this way, but could the photograph please remain on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, I wanted to ask you something else. In this yard where Batusha's cowshed is, there is yet another building which can be seen here without a roof. Am I right? Or if that is inconvenient for you, if you cannot see it there --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 3D121, page 3?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you wish a record made of the photograph that's on the screen at the moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC69, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's have 3D121.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 3D121, page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, this is a picture of the yard where Batusha's cowshed was. According to the information I have, the building on the left-hand side should be Batusha's house, but my question to you is the following: The building in the middle of the yard, who does that belong to; do you know?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It belongs to Qazim Batusha, the one without a roof. I think this photograph was recently made; it's not from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Correct. It was recently taken, this photograph, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Could we have an indication from the Defence when that was taken?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 25th of May, 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, the building on the left-hand side, who does that belong to?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Beli Avdyli. This one here, it's Beli Avdyli's house. But this photograph was also recently taken because this wall wasn't here before.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 3D121, pages 1 and 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, is it correct that NATO aircraft bombed your village twice during the war, on the 13th of May, 1999, and on the 2nd of June, 1999; to be more precise, the wine cellar, "vinarija," by the asphalt road?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time while I was there, NATO did not bomb. NATO bombed on the 24th in the evening, but that was far from our house. We could only see the planes, the aircraft, going in that direction, but they did not bomb the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: When you came back - and you said that you came back in June 1999 - did you see --

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: June --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: -- the effects of the bombing of the wine cellar?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No effects of the bombing in the village, only in the cellar. You could see some effects there, but not in the village. When we came back from Albania, we observed this.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ramadani, Aziz Shehu, one of the persons on your list, was he employed in the wine cellar; do you know, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, one more question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Which list was that, Mr. Visnjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that's the list that the witness provided --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] to the Court, and that person is mentioned on that list. I haven't got the exact number of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: One of the victims?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, one of the victims, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I appreciate --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P2537 [as interpreted], that's what my colleague said to me just now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I appreciate that that's the list, but it had a number of different categories and there also was a list of other people given separately from that document. But anyway, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I haven't got the document in front of me now, but I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You don't need the document. I just wanted to know what list you're referring to. I'm quite content with the explanation, thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, I just note a mistake in the transcript. The exhibit number says 2537, but it's 2337.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, I didn't realise that's why --

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: 2357 is the correct number, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I didn't realise that that's what the registrar was drawing my attention to, but he had spotted it already. Thanks for the clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, to the best of your knowledge, is it correct that all Albanians from your village left the village on the 26th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the women left on the 26th of March. The men, they all remained in the village and they were all burned. From 13 years of age and elderly persons, they were burned.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, only Serbs stayed behind in the village, and the Roma. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have that exhibit, P2357, on the screen, please. And can we go to the next page. I'm sorry, it must be yet another page over, please. It's one of the shorter lists I'm looking for. Over again, please. That's it. Yes. Thank you very much. You can remove that. Ms. Moeller.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Just a few questions, Your Honour. Could we call up P99, page 2 again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, this is the photo we just looked at already this morning, and you already pointed out on this picture where your house was in relation to the asphalt road, but it wasn't marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Could the usher assist with a pen.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And could you try to mark it. Should we move in a little bit before we do that, towards the asphalt road, or do you feel you can do it in this perspective?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why can't we use the one where it was already marked, which was IC -- I can't remember the number. But we had the house marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: No, we had the asphalt -- Mr. Visnjic had the Batusha barn side road, but not where he lived, from where he saw the asphalt road in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So it was marked on an earlier -- on a different photograph. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, do you see your house on this, or shall we zoom in a little bit?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No problem. This is the house. And from here you can see the Prizren-Gjakova main road. It's in the outskirts of the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Could you also make a line on this road that you just talked about, the Gjakova-Prizren road? Or could you make dots where your saw armoured vehicles and tanks that morning from your house, just some red dots on the road.

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see everything from here, from my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And, as the crow flies, how much is the distance between your house and this road, approximately?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I do apologise, but I'm not an expert in knowing these distances, as the crow flies. But I could say it was 500 or 600 metres, maybe even less, 400 metres, as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Could we take a snap-shot of this picture, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC70, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, do you know what a T-55 tank is?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see the numbers, because I could not verify the exact number from here, whether it was 55 or another asphalt -- or another number.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: I assume it is a specific tank model, and my question would be: Would you have the knowledge to distinguish different kinds of military tanks from each other?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you show me the pictures, I can distinguish different kinds. If you show me pictures of tanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: But could you describe, without seeing any picture, what a T-55 tank actually is, how such a tank looks like? Or are you unfamiliar with these specifications?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, I'm a farmer; I'm not an expert in these things. I cannot draw a tank and all its differences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think we understand the point, Ms. Moeller --

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- but one of the weaknesses of it is that it was your investigator who asked the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, you said that armoured vehicles also entered the village. Could you show on this picture where you saw them closer to the village or in the village? And could the usher give you a pen.

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This road goes inside the village and links up with this road here. It's a crossroads, but you cannot see it from the trees. There are trees now; there weren't trees then. So it is along these houses. Tanks were here and here, those that I saw. But people said that there were tanks on this side as well, but I didn't see that myself. I'm only testifying about things that I saw.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Is this a clear marking, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it's an answer to a question that wasn't asked, because, as I understand it, it was APCs which were in the village and now you've got an answer about tanks being somewhere different from the answers we've had already. So I think it would be helpful if you could clarify it, and if you could also clarify what the various "heres" we're referring to, because they don't show up on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, could you assist the Judges. The two dots that you made towards the direction of the village from the asphalt road, what vehicles did you see there? What kind of vehicles?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've already explained that. The armoured vehicles were on this road here, while the tanks and the Pragas were along the asphalt road. These were here at the entrance into the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Can you draw a bigger line where you saw the armoured vehicles going and up to which point.

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The armoured vehicle was parked here. It was parked here. This road goes to Krusha e Madhe. You cannot see it from the trees. At that time in March, the trees were not in bloom. You could see it. So this road goes inside the village as well, and also to the cellar and to Krusha e Madhe. These are the crossroads that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Could you put a 1 to the places where you saw the armoured vehicles, not the tanks but the APCs.

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The armoured vehicles here, 1, and here, 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Ramadani, to torture you with that longer, but it's not really clearly visible on the screen. Could you maybe make a cross at the points which you just drafted where you saw the APCs so that it's clearly distinguishable from the other things.

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's clear. This road passes through the asphalt road and enters into the village. It goes to Krusha e Madhe, this road, and it's not an asphalt road. This is a crossroads. The road goes into the village, to the cellar, and to Krusha e Madhe. The tank was here and here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think that -- you can just wipe that map off -- well -- yes, it seems to me we should start again this exercise, if you want to go through it, because I think we're all completely confused now.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes. Could we start with a fresh -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman. Just hold on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, if the purpose is clarification, it's clearly not working. And I also wonder if this is appropriate re-direct, since the question of vehicles and their location is covered in his statement and should have been covered on direct if it was important to the Prosecution. I don't think it's appropriate re-direct to start with. It's more like direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that can't be so in light of the

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: try to deal with that issue, which is what I understand is happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But I think it's fair to keep that -- well, let's take a shot of this --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- as a court exhibit because it reflects the difficulties that were being experienced in dealing with this evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC71, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And then let's have a fresh copy of this exhibit on the screen. That's page 2 of P99.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Bear in mind that there's just a possibility - although I don't know if it's the case - there's just a possibility that there's an interpretational difficulty here as well and that it's important to be very clear -- that you clearly identify the vehicles that you are asking the witness to locate on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes, I will try so, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, could you now, first of all, draw a line from the street that leads from the Djakovica-Prizren road into your village. And you can draw it over the parts where you can't see the street because of the trees. But can you just indicate from the main road into your village by drawing a red line so that it gets understandable for us where this road goes. Just one continuing line, please.

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know that road very well. Maybe it's not clear to you, but I know it very well. This road goes like this. From here it turns here, to Krusha e Madhe; on this side it continues along this line. This is Dimitrije's house, where the police was stationed. And then it links up with this road here and with this one here. So this road goes to Batush, this road goes here, and this one goes to these houses here. And then up here and up to the asphalt road. So this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So that's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- the road which again links up here with the main road Prizren-Gjakova. I think it's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That is very clear now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, it is very clear now. And, Mr. Ramadani, could you now make a cross wherever, on this road that you just showed, you saw an armoured vehicle, an APC. Not a military tank, but an armoured vehicle.

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: An armoured vehicle, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you make a big cross where you saw them.

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Anywhere else? Or are these the spots where you saw them?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were also at the wine cellar, but I couldn't see that from my house. This part can be seen from my house. There is an entry road from the main road here, on this side. So this is the side that I could see from my house, and I saw these two here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The record should reflect that there are two crosses; one is near to the junction with the main road and the other one is more or less at the end of the road, leading towards the right of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ramadani, could you make a circle where you saw military tanks.

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot see Suka Brdo from here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: May the record reflect that the witness drew four circles on the right-hand upper corner on the main road Gjakova-Prizren, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ramadani, when you drew the streets -- the road into your village, you also made a tiny dot where Nikolic's house was, where you said the police was at. Could you put a triangle where you indicated this location.

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Dimitrije's house. I will mark it with a cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. And can you make a circle around this cross, please, the cross you just drafted.

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: May the record reflect that the witness put a cross with a circle around it at the location where Nikolic's house was, where the police was at. And I think that should clarify now the issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Could we take a snap-shot, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC72, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And we can remove the exhibit from the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, in cross-examination you mentioned that Dimitrije Nikolic had a kind of cafe in the village and that Serbs used to gather there. Did you see people in uniform gathering there, or were all these people in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is where they drew up their plans. They went there in the morning, the young people of the village. Then the policemen came with uniform. When the children went to school, when our children went to school, they threatened them with their guns: "Why do you go to school? What are you looking for? Are you asking for Americans and NATO?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, that's not the question you were asked, and this is important at this stage in the evidence. We can't take account of this additional material that you are presenting now because of the procedure that we follow here. It's important you listen --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- you listen to the question. And the question was: "Did you see people in uniform gathering at this cafe, or were the people who went there in civilian clothes?" Now, could you concentrate your answer on that answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both civilians and uniformed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And when did you see those two groups of people gathered there, on what dates, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 1996 they used to meet there regularly, in the afternoon. During the day the police stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And on the 25th, in the morning, did you also see people civilian clothes and uniforms gathered there?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 25th we did not dare to leave the house. It was just to escape that we left. We went towards the stream. There were gun-shots, and it was impossible to go out and see because of the bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, one last question. In cross-examination a name was mentioned, Nebojsa Nikolic. Do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nebojsa Nikolic? It's not Nebojsa Nikolic but Nebojsa Djordjevic, I think. Nebojsa Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who was this person that you referred to? Was he from Mala Krusa, Krusha e Vogel?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from Krusha e Vogel.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And do you know where he worked?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He worked in Prizren. Well, they could choose where they wanted to work because they did not have problems with employment. He worked in Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know what was his profession?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Earlier he was a driver, Nebojsa. He had a truck, but he also wore a uniform. A car -- he was also a car mechanic, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you see him on the 25th or the 26th of March in your village?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't see on the 25th whether he was there or not. Maybe he was, but I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think that completes my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Ramadani, what kind of uniform did he wear?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I explained earlier that they wore all kinds of uniforms. They wore army uniforms, police uniforms, all kinds of uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The problem with your earlier evidence is that you plainly called a person Nebojsa Nikolic, and you now seem to be clarifying that. That's why you're being asked more questions about the person. So could you tell me again what uniforms you saw him wearing?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Earlier he was a driver, a civilian. And sometime later I saw him wearing police uniforms, not the army uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, is that all you saw him wearing?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the police, not the army uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yesterday in your evidence you said that he sometimes wore paramilitary clothes. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said earlier that they would wear all kinds of clothes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. I understand that, but it's him alone I'm interested in. Did you ever see him wearing paramilitary clothes?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, even paramilitary and police uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, in the course of that re-examination there have been exhibits produced. Does any counsel seek to cross-examine further in this instance? No. Thank you. Well, Mr. Ramadani, that completes your evidence --

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honours, excuse me, could I ask one question in relation to the one question you asked?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is the question you want to ask?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: It refers to paramilitary clothes, because I'm not sure what is meant by "paramilitary uniform". I think he referred to camouflage and black uniforms, but I cannot recall we talked about paramilitary uniforms before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The wording I have noted from yesterday's evidence is "sometimes paramilitary clothes". Now --

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: I'm not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- do you disagree that that was the evidence yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: I think it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you don't think it was?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether it was clarified, what was meant by that. But I'm in Your Honour's hands for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thinking only, Mr. Ramadani, of the person you've now called Nebojsa Djordjevic, when you say that you have seen him in a paramilitary uniform, could you describe that, please.

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not very good with colours. Colours were various. There were camouflage, you know, multi-coloured clothes; blue uniforms, black uniforms. They were not quite black, but I call them black.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, it may be important that you're clear in your mind that we're asking about paramilitary uniform, not police uniform at this stage, paramilitary, and in relation only to that one person, Djordjevic. So what's your final answer about the description of the paramilitary uniform that you have seen him wear?

utterances.speaker: LUTFI RAMADANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The paramilitary uniform was kind of multi-coloured, not exactly blue. I don't know what to call it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, thank you, Mr. Ramadani. That does complete your evidence. It's important that you understand that while, naturally, you're principally concerned in your mind with the tragic events that you've described to us, we have to concentrate here on trying to identify if there is some person to be held accountable for these events, and that's why questions have concentrated on different issues from the ones that you might see as the most important ones. But rest assured that we're concentrating on the job of trying to identify whether crimes have been committed and whether there are persons to be held accountable for these crimes. So thank you, once again, for coming to the Tribunal to give your evidence. You're now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you very much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Moeller.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness is Mr. Mehmet Krasniqi, who formerly called himself Mehmet Avdyli.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And this is the same event?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: This is the same event. He is another one of the six survivors of this killing and his evidence relates to the same paragraphs as Mr. Ramadani's evidence. I don't know whether you want me to repeat them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You don't need to, and we have a transcript and a statement in this instance, or statements, rather.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. He is a 92 ter witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: -- formerly 92 bis (D).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration to tell the truth by reading aloud the document which will now be placed before you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Now, Mr. Krasniqi, you're going to be asked questions to clarify points in the evidence you gave before, perhaps to challenge that evidence, and also to add certain information to that evidence. The important thing to remember is that we've got all this evidence that you've given before in front of us and we want to concentrate on anything extra that you can say to clarify it or to add to it rather than go back over the same area again, because we already know what you have said before. So please concentrate on the particular question that's being asked and try to confine your answer to the point that is recognised by the question. The first person to ask you questions will be for the Prosecutor, and that will be Ms. Moeller. Ms. Moeller.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Can you state your name for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Mehmet Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Was your last name formerly Avdyli?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And when did you change your name from Avdyli to Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I changed it in 1999 because my brother, my father, and my sister had the surname Krasniqi, while I had formerly my grandfather's surname, Avdyli. Later on I decided to take the surname of my father, my brother, and my sister, Krasniqi, as the surname of our whole family.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And because you changed your last name in 1999, did you sign some statements that you provided to investigators of this Tribunal with the last name Avdyli and others with the last name Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, some said that I should keep the former surname, but I wanted to keep the surname Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Sir, when you came here this week, did you show representatives of this Office of the Prosecutor your picture ID card?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, to all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Krasniqi, where are you from?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Krusha e Vogel, municipality of Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And where did you live in March 1999?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Until the 26th of March, I was in Krusha e Vogel.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Are you married?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. I've got three children.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And what is your profession?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Farmer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, did you give a statement to investigators of this Tribunal on 4 April 1999?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, in Kukes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And at this point was also a video taken of your injuries that you had at the time?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. I was signing things, and also they took photographs of my face and hands.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to play a short video-clip. It's 90 seconds. It's Exhibit P2243 and it's a contemporaneous video taken on 4 April 1999, when the witness was interviewed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: "Today is 4 April 1999, the time is ten to 8.00 in the evening. We are in Kukes with the witness Mehmet Avdyli. He is a witness that comes from Kosovo, from the village of Krusha e Vogel. He sustained ... he allegedly sustained his injuries and burn injuries from being put into a house by Serb policemen, and eventually surviving the attack where 110 people perished. They were shot and later burned to death. We are now in a position to place the injuries on a videotape to file as evidence. "Can you tell me what your name is? "Mehmet Avdyli. "And where do you come from? "[Voiceover] From Krusha e Vogel, municipality of Prizren."

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: There's a second small clip.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, how was your condition at that time? That was roughly less than ten days after the incident.

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: My condition?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes. How did you feel at that time? How was your physical state?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, I had fever, was in a lot of pain, all these things. But I thanked God that I was able to survive from the massacre. So I felt better that I was alive, because all the rest died, perished, and their remains have not been found to this day. They just disappeared.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Krasniqi, did you give a further statement to the Tribunal in 2001, on 5 October?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And on 7 March 2002, did you sign a declaration in which you declared that both the statements you had given before were true and correct, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. I've given statements. I've given statements to the people from the Tribunal, and I've told the whole truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes. And when you were seen in 2002, did you make some corrections to the two statements you had given previously, and were two addendums made in this regard?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I think so. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: When you came here this week, did you have the opportunity to read through the two statements and the two addendums?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't remember. It's been a long time, four years ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: No, I think we misunderstood each other. This week, when you arrived here in The Hague, were you shown your previous statements, four altogether?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes. All of them. I thought I did not understand the question correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes. And did you look through all of them, read through them, or have them read to you?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, we read all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And do you declare today to these honourable Judges that these statements accurately reflect your testimony, and if you would testify today, that you would say the same?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Exactly the same. I've always said the same things, the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point I would like to tender Exhibit P2341, which are the statements and the declaration, and Exhibit P2243, which is the short video-clip shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Should we deal with the transcript now as well?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going on to that. I just have to correct myself. The video is Exhibit P2343.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, in 2002 did you come here to this Tribunal and testify in the trial against Slobodan Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And do you declare that you gave a true and correct testimony then in this trial?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, the whole truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: I would also wish to tender Exhibit P2342, which is the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, is that a convenient moment to interrupt?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: I think it would be, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Krasniqi, we need to have a break now and we will be resuming at 11.00. The usher will show you to where you can wait meanwhile, so can you please leave the court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And we shall resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, your evidence will now continue. Ms. Moeller.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, in your statement, you said that on 25 March, in the morning, you were awoken by tanks close to your houses. What kind of tanks were these? Were they military tanks?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Military and all kinds of tanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: What were the other kinds of tanks that you mean by "all kinds," if you know?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Tanks, armoured vehicles, Pragas, heavy artillery.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And how close were they to the houses in the village where you were?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Along the Prizren-Gjakova main asphalt road, they were there, because this road runs in the outskirts of the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And how far away, approximately, was your house from this road?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: About 250 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Did you see that day also any persons in uniforms entering your village?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: That day, on Thursday, in the morning the entire population fled to the mountain, and I didn't see any that morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And on the next morning, on the 26th of March, you say in your statement that a group of 15 policemen made you and the others come out of the woods. How did these policemen look? What did they wear?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: They had different uniforms; camouflage uniforms and military clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: What colour had their military clothes, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: They had this dark yellow colour with a pattern.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: When you say "yellow" -- or let me ask differently. What colour is the shirt that you wear today?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: This colour it was, but darker, much darker, and with a pattern. And the other was grass colour with a pattern, the military colour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may the record reflect that the witness is wearing a blue shirt with some white stripes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, that day of 26th March, when the killing in the Batusha cowshed occurred, did you notice Serb villagers that you knew from before being present there?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: At that moment we couldn't see that because we were made to put our hands behind our heads and kneel. And only when we were taken to the cowshed and executed, a student, Shefqet Shehu from Krusha e Vogel, who studied in Pristina, he stood up after the shots were fired and saw a Serb from the village, from the window. He had a fire-arm, his weapon. And he said to them, "Momcilo, neighbour, you are doing this?" And he opened fire again until he ran out of bullets.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And where were you when Shefqet Shehu said these words? Where were you in relation to him, to Shefqet?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I was in that room, in the same room where the bodies fell on me. I kept silent because the bodies were on me. I had Muharrem Asllani behind me and he was really heavy. And Zenun Adnani bled on me. I was -- I could hear the screams and cries of people who were injured; some lightly and some seriously. And after that they set the cowshed on fire. They threw this kind of liquid; it had a very strange smell. I was there until they started to put straw and hay on the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Let me stop you here for a second. I was just trying to clarify whether you heard, yourself, Shefqet Shehu saying these words, "Momcilo, neighbour, you're doing this?" Did you hear that yourself?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I heard it myself. I was in the same room with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And who do you think he was referring to when he said "Momcilo"?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: He was referring to a Serb from the village whom he knew.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And would you know what was the last name of this Momcilo?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Momcilo Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you. But you, yourself, at that moment, you didn't look around. You didn't see Momcilo Nikolic yourself, did you?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, I couldn't see him because the bodies were on my back. After they put the hay on the bodies, I was on the ground when the smoke came. I said to myself, "It's better for me to leave this room and better to die from a bullet than from this fire." So when I was leaving the cowshed, I didn't have time to stop and look.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you -- after you managed to leave the shed which was on fire, you stated that you retreated into the forest and stayed in the vicinity of your village for about two days. What did you observe going on in the village in these two days?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: The Serbs from the village were collecting hay and they were putting the hay on the bodies for the bodies to be burned.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: During these two days, were there also uniformed persons still in the village that you did not know, who were not Serbs from the village?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I was in the mountains. I didn't dare go out during the day. In the evenings, I couldn't go any nearer to the village. I just wanted to go as far as possible from it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: So could you actually recognise who were the persons who put more hay on the bodies in the cowshed, or was it too far away?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It was far away. It was also dark. They were about 150 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Krasniqi, I would now go with you to the point when you arrived in Nagavc. You said in your statement that you were treated by a Dr. Xhemal Dana. Were you treated by any other doctor in Nagavc while you were there?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: When I went to Nagavc village, I met Dr. Ali Hoti. He treated me that day with scarce medicaments he had. And after some time I met Xhemal Dana in another house in Nagavc but he didn't have any medicine. Therefore, for the days I spent in Nagavc, up to the 2nd of April, he treated me with natural medicine. He would put yoghurt on my hands to take the fever away.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. Krasniqi, in the first statement you gave very close to the events, you included a list of the men who were with you in the barn and who, according to your knowledge, died in this barn. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It is fully correct, because to this day their own children ask themselves where the bodies of their fathers are. Every child wonders where the grave of his father is, and we don't know where their graves are, where their traces are, where their bones lie.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And in this list, you also referred to Lutfi Ramadani being among them. At that time, on 4 April 1999, did you know that Lutfi Ramadani was alive? Did you see him during these events, or at any time before you gave the statement?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: When we were taken to the cowshed where we were executed and set on fire, I know that everybody went in that room. But when I left, I knew that I was the only one who left. I didn't know at that time that Lutfi and certain other persons left the room as well. It is six of us who survived that massacre.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And did you also advise the Office of the Prosecutor in a later statement that you gave that one more person that was in your first statement, a young boy called Sefer Batusha, was not dead but alive.

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to point out at this stage that Schedule C does contain the name of Sefer Batusha. The schedules were reviewed when we amended the indictment, but that name must have slipped through. So we will not lead evidence, of course, in regard to him being dead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So should we delete that name from the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. The position is noted, Ms. Moeller.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, when did you return to Mala Krusa after this event, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I returned on the 26th of June, at 2.00 a.m. In a car with a cousin of mine - my wife and children were with me - we all returned to Krusha e Vogel.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And have you lived in Krusha e Vogel since?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And apart from Lutfi Ramadani and Sefer Batusha, have you seen any of the men you listed in your statement being alive since you last saw them in the Batusha cowshed?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, they were not seen alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And have any of the relatives, who live in your village, of these men ever said anything to the effect that they saw any of their relatives being alive?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No. Nobody said that they were alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: After you returned to Krusha e Vogel, did you go back to the Batusha barn or cowshed?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. Together with some people from the village who asked me about those people, we went there to see. We found some remains of a skull, remains of ribs and legs, and some shoes. They had cleaned the place and they had mined it. And the place is -- to this date, you can see that it was mined. There is a hole. And we have also found cartridges.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And do you know what happened to the cowshed?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: They had carried all the concrete blocks to Drini. Some men from the village had found some remains there as well, and they could identify 14 bodies, other bodies except -- in addition to the 100 and more bodies of those men that I've mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I noticed that I've reached the 30 minutes. I would, with your leave, like to show this witness one picture of the Drini River and I would have one final question for him after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't understand the last answer, Ms. Moeller. "They had carried all the concrete blocks to Drini."

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes, I would like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that the men from the village?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: -- I would like to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, who do you mean when you say, "They carried the concrete blocks to the Drini"? Who were "they"?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Those who cleaned the area, who burned all those men, they took everything - the remains, the blocks - to Drini River, the Serbs from the village. I was not there to see who exactly did that, but it was the Serbs from the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Could we call up Exhibit 102, page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, could you have a look at this picture and say whether you recognise that.

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, this is Drini River.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And did you go there after you returned to your village?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Not to the place where they brought these concrete blocks. I couldn't go there. I didn't feel very well to go and see things that reminded me of what had happened in the village. Other men from the village went there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And it was these men who told you about it?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Krasniqi, my two last questions are: How is the situation today in Krusha e Vogel for the people there?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Today the population has decreased in Krusha e Vogel. The 100 and more people that were massacred are unaccounted for. Children have grown up. They have started to go to school, started to work. This is how I can describe it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Okay. And how are you feeling today, Mr. Krasniqi, after all you went through?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't feel well, but I believe in God and I took an oath before God to look after myself because I really don't feel very well. I have gone through a lot. Whenever I discuss the massacre that occurred in the village with anyone, I feel the trauma that I suffered.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will follow the indictment, and I have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that Mr. O'Sullivan made a mistake. I'm supposed to go last. I've just spoken to my colleague Mr. Lukic now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Thank you. We have no questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'll have just a few questions for this witness. Sorry, I have a technical problem as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Krasniqi. I'm Djuro Cepic, one of the lawyers in the Defence team for Mr. Lazarevic. I would like to ask you a few questions. I'll try and be very specific and very clear, and I would kindly ask for short answers. Amongst other statements, you gave a statement on the 5th of October, 2001, to the investigators of the ICTY, and in that statement you describe the uniforms that were carried by the persons on the 26th of March. And, amongst other things, you said that -- you said that there were certain people in blue camouflage uniforms and that they entered Dimitrije Nikolic's house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Further on you describe certain people as wearing green camouflage uniforms and white bands, and you did not see any insignia on those uniforms. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Further on you describe a group of people who wore a combination of green camouflage trousers and shirts, and you did not see any insignia on those uniforms either. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, I did not see any insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The last group of people also did not wear anything on their heads. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No. I didn't see anyone with hats.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Some of them sported moustaches or beards. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, there were people with beards, not very big beards, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And they ranged in age between 30 and 40. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now display Exhibit 99 and the picture on which the last two digits are 06. Do I need to -- okay, then. Thank you. Could Mr. Krasniqi please be assisted.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Here, in this photo, we see your village, Mala Krusa. Mr. Krasniqi, can you show your house on this photo, please.

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: If you could enlarge it a little bit, because I can't see very well. Here. My house is this one here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you mark it by number 1, please.

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: So this is up the road here. You mean -- shall I mark the street or the house?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just the house, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- are you going to be asking for other things to be marked on this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that will do, I think, for present purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, from your house to the asphalt road, from Djakovica to Prizren, is some 4 to 500 metres as the crow flies. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, it's not 400 metres away. I have not measured the distance, but I gave you an estimation. I don't know what the exact figure would be, but my estimation would be 250 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement given on the 4th of April, 1999, on page 2, in paragraph 4, you say that around 3.00 in the morning you were woken up by the tanks that had appeared on that road. At 3.00 in the morning it was dark, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And from that distance from your house, you could not see the Djakovica-Prizren road at 3.00 in the morning when it was still dark. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I could see them because they had lights on, and there was such a big noise that we heard. And when they stopped, we could see everything from the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And before that, did you hear a loud detonation and the sound of aeroplanes flying above you on that same night?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET KRASNIQI
